h1: The 6 Best Office Storage Carts With Drawers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Office Storage Carts 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six rolling storage carts with drawers, from 4-drawer slim carts to 10-drawer towers, compared on capacity, casters and size.
summary: The LEHOM 8-drawer cart is the best office storage cart with drawers: stated 33 lb top and 11 lb per-drawer limits, a flat wooden top and partial caster locking. The 10-drawer cart adds capacity, the SYKIARIOL is the shorter color-coded option, and the IRIS is the compact Made in USA pick. The mesh 4-drawer and Goovilla serve tools and craft.
intro: Rolling carts all look alike in photos, and the product pages bury the specs that decide whether one earns floor space: how much each drawer holds, how many casters lock, and how much footprint it claims beside a desk. A cart that rolls away while you tug a drawer open, or sags under a ream of paper, fails at its one job.

We ranked six drawer carts from our pool. A laptop charging cart and a duplicate listing of the 10-drawer model were dropped, because neither fits the title or adds a distinct pick. Scores come from listing specs only, so cart dimensions and stated weight limits weighed heavily, and a missing limit counted against the cart, since a drawer with no rating is a guess.

products.name: LEHOM Rolling Storage Cart with 8 Drawers, Utility Cart on Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: Clear weight limits and a flat top in the $25-50 bucket.
products.description:
The LEHOM stands 31.18 inches tall on a 15.55 by 12.60 inch footprint, with eight drawers and a wooden flat top. It states 33 lb on the top plate and 11 lb per drawer. Published limits are rare on cheap carts, and they let you judge whether paper reams or tool bits are safe in each drawer before the runners bind.

It beats the SYKIARIOL because both list the same weights, but this one costs less, in the $25 to $50 bucket, and stands taller. Partial locking casters steady the cart while you open a drawer.

Buy it if you want the most drawers for the least money. The caveat is the 11 lb per-drawer limit, which rules out dense items like stacked binders, and only some casters lock.
products.idealFor: Home offices that need lots of small drawers cheaply.

products.name: 10 Drawers Rolling Cart with Wooden Tabletop, Utility Storage Cart with Wheels
products.verdict: Ten drawers and a scratch-resistant top, with tool-free assembly.
products.description:
This 10-drawer cart pairs a waterproof, scratch-resistant wooden tabletop with four 360 degree casters, two with brakes, and tool-free assembly. Ten drawers suit sorted categories: screws, labels, cables, craft supplies. A waterproof top shrugs off spilled coffee, which a bare laminate top would not.

It ranks second because it costs a tier more than the LEHOM, in the $50 to $100 bucket, for two extra drawers, and the listing gives no dimensions or per-drawer weights. Half-locking casters demand the same care with loading as the LEHOM.

Choose it for papers, parts or craft supplies spread over many categories. The caveat is uncertainty: without listed size, measure your space first, and skip it if four drawers would do.
products.idealFor: People with many categories of small items.

products.name: SYKIARIOL Rolling Storage Cart with Drawers, 8 Drawers Utility Cart, Black
products.verdict: A shorter 8-drawer cart with color-coded drawers and a rust-resistant frame.
products.description:
The SYKIARIOL measures 15.55 by 12.60 by 25.47 inches with eight color-coded drawers, and lists the same 33 lb top and 11 lb per-drawer limits as the LEHOM. A rust-resistant frame and video-guided assembly round out the package. At 25.47 inches, it is the shortest cart here with listed dimensions, so it slides under many tables.

It trails the LEHOM because the weights match, but this one is shorter and costs a tier more, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Color coding speeds up sorting but does nothing for capacity.

Buy it if you want to sort items by color or need under-table storage. The caveat is value: if height is not a constraint, the LEHOM gives more cart for less money.
products.skipIf: You want more height for less money.

products.name: IRIS USA 4-Drawer Rolling Storage Cart with Organizer Top, Black/Pearl
products.verdict: A compact Made in USA cart with an organizer top and drawer stops.
products.description:
The IRIS cart measures 14.25 by 12.05 by 26.44 inches, with four drawers, an organizer top, built-in drawer stops and removable wheels. It is Made in USA. Drawer stops prevent the drawer from sliding all the way out and dumping its contents, which cheap carts often lack.

It ranks below the eight-drawer carts because it offers half the drawers at a similar $25 to $50 price. Its advantages are the narrowest footprint here, the organizer top and the stops, so it fits tight gaps beside a desk.

Pick it for a narrow desk-side spot. The caveat is that no weight limits are listed, so treat the drawers as light-duty, and skip it if you need many compartments.

products.name: Rolling Cart with Drawers, 4-Drawer Storage Cart on Wheels with Wooden Top, Metal
products.verdict: Mesh drawers and a 150 lb frame rating for visible storage.
products.description:
This four-drawer metal cart has a wooden top, a 150 lb frame capacity and mesh drawers each measuring 12 by 16.5 by 4.25 inches. Mesh lets you see contents without opening anything, which is useful for tools, chargers and loose supplies you grab fast. The metal frame suggests sturdier construction than the plastic-drawer carts.

It ranks fifth because the 150 lb figure is a frame rating, not a per-drawer limit, so you still do not know what a single drawer holds. The mesh gives visibility the solid drawers lack, in the same $25 to $50 bucket.

Buy it for tools and supplies you want to spot quickly. The caveat is depth: 4.25 inches limits what fits, and tiny items can slip through the mesh.

products.name: Goovilla Rolling Cart with 5 Drawers for Craft, Art, Dorm, Office, White
products.verdict: Three shallow and two deep drawers in white, with a 40 lb top.
products.description:
The Goovilla has five drawers, three shallow and two deep, in white with a 40 lb tabletop rating. The drawers detach and have pull-out limiters, with 11 lb per drawer. Mixed depths solve an annoying problem: shallow drawers for pens and tape, deep ones for paint tubes or glue guns.

It lands last because the listing gives no size, and it holds fewer drawers than the bigger carts. The 40 lb top rating is the highest top limit here, ahead of the LEHOM's 33 lb, which helps if you plan to set a printer on it.

Choose it for a dorm or craft corner. The caveat is the missing dimensions: check the size against your space before you buy, because you cannot confirm fit from the listing alone.

whatMatters.detail: A cart lists how much its top and each drawer can hold, as the LEHOM does with 33 lb and 11 lb. It matters because overloaded drawers sag or jam, and runners fail first. Look for lb numbers in the bullets, and treat a missing limit as a reason to be cautious about heavy items. Spread weight evenly across drawers.

Casters are the wheels, and locking ones stop the cart rolling. It matters most when you pull a drawer open, since the cart tends to follow your hand. Read how many of the four wheels lock, because partial locking, as on the LEHOM and the 10-drawer cart, steadies less than full locking would. Test the brakes by pushing the loaded cart.

The width and depth decide whether the cart fits beside your desk or under a table. Measure the gap first, including clearance for the drawers to open. The listing gives length, width and height, and the SYKIARIOL's 25.47 inch height is the lowest listed here. Missing dimensions, as on the Goovilla, are a warning sign.

A shallow drawer holds papers and cables but not bulky items, while a deep one takes tubes, tape rolls or tools. Match depth to what you store. Check drawer dimensions, not just overall size, as the mesh cart's 4.25 inch depth shows, because overall height hides how shallow each compartment really is.

Tool-free or video-guided assembly saves time and avoids stripped screws. It matters if you dislike hardware or have limited tools. The listing often states how the cart is put together, as with the 10-drawer cart's tool-free build and the SYKIARIOL's video guide. Expect more steps with eight drawers than with four, and keep a screwdriver nearby.

faq.q: Why was the charging cart excluded?
faq.a: It is a laptop charging station, not a drawer storage cart, so it does not match the title. Including it would have mixed two different products in one ranking and muddied the comparison between drawer counts and limits.

faq.q: How much can each drawer hold?
faq.a: The LEHOM, SYKIARIOL and Goovilla list 11 lb per drawer. The IRIS and the 10-drawer cart state no per-drawer limit, so treat them as light-duty storage for papers, cables and small supplies rather than heavy items.
Not on every model. The LEHOM has partial locking and the 10-drawer cart has two brakes on four casters. Park either one against a wall if you plan to pull the drawers hard, so the cart cannot drift.

faq.q: Is the 10-drawer cart worth it over the 8-drawer?
faq.a: Only if you need two extra categories. It costs a tier more than the LEHOM, and the listing gives no dimensions, so confirm the footprint before choosing the larger cart for a tight corner.

faq.q: Which cart fits under a desk?
faq.a: The SYKIARIOL, at 25.47 inches tall, is the shortest cart with listed dimensions. The IRIS follows at 26.44 inches, and both are compact enough to slide under many tables. Measure your clearance first.

faq.q: Do mesh drawers hold small items?
faq.a: They show contents, but the drawers on the mesh cart are shallow at 4.25 inches, so tiny loose items such as screws or beads can slip through. Use a small tray inside to keep them contained.

finalTake: For most home offices, the LEHOM 8-drawer cart is the right pick: clear weight limits, a flat wooden top and low cost. Choose the 10-drawer cart for sorted supplies, the SYKIARIOL for under-table height, and the IRIS for narrow gaps. Check the stated drawer limits and caster locking before buying, and measure the space first.
